### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

> "A card came with my plan papers back in September and nobody has told me what it is for. I want to know whether I am owed anything on it."

- Target object: the card that came with the plan papers, and what is owed on it.
- Timing: now; nothing in the script defers anything.
- Boundary: he asks only to be told. "He does not ask for anything to be done to the card and would not know what to ask
  for; he is content for the plan to do whatever its own side of the work is, and says so if he is asked for that."
- Authorisation: "If the representative explains that bringing the card into use is something only he can do and hands
  it over to him, he does it there and then"; and "If the representative tells him that something has to be put right on
  the card's record before anything can be put on it, he says to go ahead and do whatever is needed."

The simulator is passive and strictly conditional. Identity elements, the card's last four digits (8802), the date the
envelope came, and the contents of the plan's letter are all released only on being asked; the letter's line —
"which sets out the benefit quarters the card runs in, 2026-Q3 and 2026-Q4" — comes out only in answer to "what does
that letter say", is given as an unordered pair, and is glossed "none of it meant anything to him", so he assigns
neither label to anything. He names no amount, no period mapping and no reference. He states plainly that he has spent
nothing ("no, not a penny") and that no statement was ever sent. He executes one `owner=user` tool when handed it, and
"raises nothing the representative has not raised with him."

### 2. Act now, wait, or refuse — and the eligibility grounds

**Act now**, after identity, and in two writes of which the first must be his.

- Identity: `verify_member_identity` — phone 4155504418, DOB 1955-02-17, MBI 3JL5RK9TN62 all match the profile.
- The card may still be brought into use: `card_activation_and_replacement_3bc5245e` — "The member activates the card no
  later than the last day of the activation window counted from the date the card was posted… Calendar days are counted
  from the day after the card was posted". The Premier row of `card_issue_and_replacement_terms_6172887b` gives 120
  calendar days; `card_issued_date` is 2026-09-04, so the window runs to 2027-01-03. 2026-10-20 is inside it. (And the
  same document adds that nothing is lost either way: "the allowance itself is never lost for want of activation".)
- He is owed something: `making_good_an_allowance_the_schedule_owed_376464e7` — "An allowance the schedule owed for a
  benefit period that has already gone by is not lost because the card was not in use when its load day passed."
- Nothing supports waiting or refusing; `find_allowance_benefit_requests` returns nothing and the programme is
  `card_issued`, not stopped or closed.

### 4. Each scored parameter — formula in words, rows, intermediates, final value

Two writes are scored. Throughout, the benefit year is 2026, so whole months run from 2026-01-01.

#### (A) Bringing the card into use — `activate_allowance_card_a5740baf` (owner **user**)

Computation document: `first_load_valuation_basis_d785adf9` — "The allowance made available is the share of that
period's allowance the card is owed, rounded to the nearest cent at the end and at no earlier step", and "It is placed
in the benefit period the programme opened in, that being the period whose allowance it is."

| Quantity | Document | Tier reached, and the record that puts him there | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| the months in a benefit period | `how_many_months_a_benefit_period_has_4fe43aba` | row 1 — "the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year and the programme opened within the benefit year". The Premier row reads "calendar quarters of the benefit year"; `program_start_date` 2026-09-01 is no later than 2026-10-20 | 3 |
| the allowance a benefit period carries | `the_allowance_a_benefit_period_carries_a11a37bf` | row 1 — "a plan in force whose tier carries a quarterly allowance larger than the card's own". Enrollment `cc7a06ec…` is `active` with no `coverage_end_date`; its tier's quarterly figure, 250, exceeds the card's 175.00 | 250.00 |
| the months of the opening period the allowance covers | `months_of_the_opening_period_covered_3017248b` | row 1 — "the card comes into use in a later period, the opening period having ended". Opening period: 8 whole months to 2026-09-01, 8 ÷ 3 → 2026-Q3. Period of coming into use: 9 whole months to 2026-10-20, 9 ÷ 3 → 2026-Q4, later. So "the whole months of the opening period that were still to run on the day the programme opened": 2026-Q3 is Jul–Sep, 2 whole months gone when 2026-09-01 fell, 3 − 2 | 1 |
| the share of that period's allowance the card is owed | `share_of_the_period_allowance_owed_6d35498e` | row 1 — "the card's tier cuts a first load to the whole months of the period left and the programme opened after the first day of its opening period". Premier's proration basis is "the period load reduced to the whole months left in the period"; within 2026-Q3, 2 whole months stand between 2026-07-01 and 2026-09-01. Row 2 is not reached: `program_end_date` is `''` | 250.00 ÷ 3 × 1 = 83.3333… |

`first_load_amount` = **83.33** (rounded once at the end);
`benefit_period` = **2026-Q3** — "the benefit period the programme opened in", the programme having opened 2026-09-01
in a year whose benefit periods run 3 months;
`card_number_last_four` = **8802** — from the programme record, and read back by the member ("reads the last four
digits, 8802");
`allowance_program_id` = `7bc19e7a-3e47-46b1-83d8-acf4fbae2701`.

*Fall-back (this document alone, plus the figures it names):* months in a benefit period = 1; months the allowance
covers = the whole of a benefit period; the allowance a benefit period carries = "the card's own tier quarterly
allowance" = 175.00; the share owed = "the whole of that period's allowance" → **175.00**. Definite, and different
from 83.33.

#### (B) Making good the allowance owed — `post_catch_up_load_838eeda2` (owner agent), **after (A)**

Computation document: `catch_up_load_reckoning_basis_dae7e7cf` — "The allowance still owed is what the schedule owed for
the benefit periods already gone, held at the ceiling on the benefit year, less what has already been made available,
never less than nothing and rounded to the nearest cent at the end and at no earlier step", with "What the schedule owed
is the share of the first benefit period the allowance is owed for, together with the whole allowance of each benefit
period from that one up to the last that has fallen due."

The same document fixes, on its own, "the allowance a benefit period carries … the quarterly allowance the member's
medical plan tier carries where that is larger than the card's own" → **250.00**, and "A benefit period runs 3 months
where the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year" → **3**.

| Quantity | Document | Tier reached, and the record that puts him there | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| the benefit periods that have passed | `counting_the_periods_that_have_passed_385b30c8` | row 1 — "its allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year, **and its record carries at least one entry**". Satisfied only once (A) has landed: before it the programme's ledger is empty. 9 whole months to 2026-10-20, so 3 whole quarters; the current period is 2026-Q4, index 3 | 3 |
| the first benefit period the allowance is owed for | `first_period_the_allowance_is_owed_for_3f2dcc93` | row 1 — "began after the first day of the benefit year, at least 1 whole month into it". `coverage_effective_date` 2026-05-01 is 4 whole months in; 4 ÷ 3 → index 1 | 2026-Q2 |
| the months of that first period owed | `months_of_the_first_period_owed_22472b99` | row 1 — "the medical plan's cover began part way through it": 2026-Q2 starts 2026-04-01 and cover began 2026-05-01, 1 whole month in. "The months owed are then the months in a benefit period less the whole months already gone by in it when that day fell", 3 − 1 | 2 |
| the last benefit period that has fallen due | `last_period_that_has_fallen_due_76730dbb` | row 1 — "the card stands in use and at least 1 whole month has passed since the programme opened". "The card stands in use where the programme's record carries the day the member brought it into use" — true only after (A); and 2026-09-01 → 2026-10-20 is 1 whole month | the current one, 2026-Q4, index 3 |
| what has already been made available | `what_has_already_been_made_available_7dd7e007` | row 1 — "at least one load, and nothing taken back for want of spending"; after (A) the card carries exactly one load entry and no expiry entry. "The loads posted are the scheduled load entries and the extra load entries on the card's running record" | 83.33 |
| the ceiling on the benefit year | `ceiling_on_the_benefit_year_5ae64037` | row 1 — "the tier sets a yearly allowance, and the medical plan is in force". Premier's "Allowance across the benefit year" is 700.00 and `cc7a06ec…` is `active`, so the premium-count row is not reached | 700.00 |

- share of the first period = 250.00 ÷ 3 × 2 = 166.6666…
- whole allowance of the periods beyond it = 250.00 × (3 − 1) = 500.00
- the schedule owed = 666.6666…
- held at the ceiling: 666.6666… ≤ 700.00, so unchanged
- less what has already been made available: 666.6666… − 83.33 = 583.3366…

`catch_up_amount` = **583.34** (rounded once at the end);
`benefit_period` = **2026-Q4** — "The allowance still owed is placed in the benefit period in which it is made
available, because it makes good several benefit periods at once and belongs to none of them alone", and the reckoning
day 2026-10-20 falls in 2026-Q4;
`source_ledger_entry_id` = the reference of the load entry created by (A) — the only load on the card, and returned in
(A)'s confirmation line; `allowance_program_id` = `7bc19e7a…`; `customer_id` = `00cdef92…`.

*A one-cent boundary I record explicitly.* "What has already been made available is the total of the loads **posted** on
the card", and a posted load carries two decimal places, so the subtrahend is 83.33 and the result is 583.34. Had the
subtrahend been the unrounded 83.3333…, the result would be 583.33. The documents say "posted", so I take **583.34**.

*Fall-back (this document alone):* the benefit periods that have passed are "the whole months of the benefit year gone
by" (9); the first period owed is "the benefit period the programme opened in"; its months owed are "the whole of a
benefit period"; the last that has fallen due is "the period before the current one"; nothing has already been made
available; and the ceiling is "the allowance a benefit period carries" = 250.00. Every reading of the mixed
month/quarter index gives a schedule owed of at least 250.00, so the ceiling binds and the figure is **250.00**.
Definite, and different from 583.34. (The mixing itself is recorded as a defect in item 7.)

### 5. Tool sequence, owners, dependencies, terminal state

| # | Tool | Owner | Depends on | Produces |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `find_customers` | agent | his telephone number | `customer_id` 00cdef92… |
| 2 | `verify_member_identity` | agent | 1 + two caller-stated facts | the pass |
| 3 | `find_allowance_programs`, then `find_allowance_card_ledger` / `find_advantage_enrollments` scoped to this programme | agent | 2 | the 2026 Premier programme, its empty ledger, the Elite Choice enrollment |
| 4 | `activate_allowance_card_a5740baf` | **user** | 3; the representative unlocks it and reads him `allowance_program_id`, `first_load_amount` 83.33 and `benefit_period` 2026-Q3 | programme in use, load entry of 83.33 in 2026-Q3, balance 83.33 |
| 5 | `post_catch_up_load_838eeda2` | agent | **4**, for three separate reasons given below | extra load of 583.34 in 2026-Q4 |

Forward dependency 4 → 5 is not merely an ordering of writes; it changes the number. Before (A):
`counting_the_periods_that_have_passed_385b30c8` falls to its third row because the programme's record carries no entry;
`last_period_that_has_fallen_due_76730dbb` falls to "no benefit period has fallen due" because the record carries no day
of coming into use; and `what_has_already_been_made_available_7dd7e007` falls to "no load at all". Computing (B) first
therefore produces a different and wrong figure. Terminal state: programme in use, balance 83.33 + 583.34 = 666.67, and
the member told what has been put on for the periods gone by.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

```
make good the allowance owed for the benefit periods already gone   (what the customer asked about)
└── the card stands in use on the programme record                  → bring the card into use (the member's own write)
```

**Hop 1 — the card must stand in use. Mark: state-derived.**
Sentence, in the blocked problem's own hub `making_good_an_allowance_the_schedule_owed_376464e7`:
> "**When the allowance is made available.** The allowance owed for the benefit periods already gone is not made available before the card stands in use on the programme record."

It names a state of the records and no action, no performer and no tool. What the state means is stated elsewhere in the
corpus in the same words, in a document of a different problem's ladder:
`last_period_that_has_fallen_due_76730dbb` — "The card stands in use where the programme's record carries the day the
member brought it into use." `find_allowance_programs` returns `card_activated_date: ''` and `status: card_issued`, so
the state does not hold. Searching on the sentence's own words — "the card", "in use", "the programme record" — reaches
`bringing_a_card_into_use_and_its_first_allowance_1f7ee466`, whose own rule describes the write that brings the state
about: "The programme is set to in use with that day recorded as the day the card was brought into use, a single load
entry on the card's running record carries the allowance made available". That document also says whose write it is —
"Only the member can do this, because only they can say the card reached them" — which is why the sequence needs the
hand-over, and the persona answers it conditionally ("If the representative explains that bringing the card into use is
something only he can do and hands it over to him, he does it there and then").

The customer said none of this. He asked whether he was owed anything; he did not ask for the card to be activated and,
by the script, "would not know what to ask for".

**No hop was pre-solved.** `making_good_an_allowance_the_schedule_owed_376464e7` names only its own tool
(`post_catch_up_load_838eeda2`, inside its own invocation block) and never names `activate_allowance_card_a5740baf`,
nor the activation problem, nor any order of writes beyond its one prerequisite sentence. Checked across the whole
published `docs/` tree: each of the six allowance tool identifiers occurs in exactly one file, its own policy's hub.

### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**The visible materials support the conclusion reached**, with one figure fetched from the sibling product the rule
names by its official title ("the member's enrollment in the Medicare Advantage Health Plans").

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes them.**

- *First load of 175.00 (the card's own quarterly allowance).* Excluded by `the_allowance_a_benefit_period_carries_a11a37bf`
  row 1, satisfied because the Elite Choice quarterly figure 250 is larger than 175.00 and the enrollment is `active`.
- *First load of 250.00 (no proration).* Excluded by `share_of_the_period_allowance_owed_6d35498e` row 1, satisfied
  because Premier's proration basis reads "the period load reduced to the whole months left in the period" and the
  programme opened 2 whole months into 2026-Q3. Row 3 ("any other case") is reached only where neither condition holds.
- *Two months of the opening period rather than one.* Excluded by `months_of_the_opening_period_covered_3017248b` row 1,
  which counts "the whole months of the opening period that were still to run **on the day the programme opened**" —
  2026-09-01, leaving September alone.
- *Swapping the two labels — 2026-Q4 on the activation and 2026-Q3 on the catch-up.* Excluded twice over by the
  documents and the records, never by the caller. `first_load_valuation_basis_d785adf9`: "It is placed in the benefit
  period the programme opened in", and `program_start_date` is 2026-09-01, which with a 3-month benefit period is
  2026-Q3. `catch_up_load_reckoning_basis_dae7e7cf`: "The allowance still owed is placed in the benefit period in which
  it is made available, because it makes good several benefit periods at once and belongs to none of them alone", and
  the reckoning day is 2026-10-20, which is 2026-Q4. The member states the two labels together, once, only when asked
  what the letter says, and attaches neither to anything ("none of it meant anything to him"); nothing in the script
  lets him be asked which goes where, and nothing lets him volunteer them.
- *First period owed = the period the programme opened in (2026-Q3).* Excluded by
  `first_period_the_allowance_is_owed_for_3f2dcc93` row 1 and by
  `making_good_an_allowance_the_schedule_owed_376464e7`: "Where a programme is opened later than the day the health plan
  carrying it began cover, it still runs for that plan's benefit year and the allowance is owed from the benefit period
  that plan's cover began in, not from the day the programme was opened."
- *Three months of 2026-Q2 owed rather than two.* Excluded by `months_of_the_first_period_owed_22472b99` row 1, cover
  having begun 2026-05-01, one whole month into the quarter.
- *Last period due = 2026-Q3 (the period before the current one).* Excluded by
  `last_period_that_has_fallen_due_76730dbb` row 1, both of whose conditions hold once the card is in use.
- *Ceiling = 250.00 (the allowance a benefit period carries).* Excluded by `ceiling_on_the_benefit_year_5ae64037` row 1,
  the Premier tier setting a yearly allowance of 700.00 and the plan being in force. The middle row, which prorates by
  "the count of premium charges raised on that enrollment over the 12 months", is closed off by `status: active`.
- *Counting the 2025 Core programme's loads as "already made available".* Excluded by the object narrowing:
  `what_has_already_been_made_available_7dd7e007` reads "the loads posted **on the card**", the card being this
  programme's; and the 2025 rows carry a different `allowance_program_id` and a different `benefit_year`.

**Counter-proof on the tree: why "do only what he asked" fails.** He asked to be told whether he is owed anything. Read
the balance and answer "nothing" and the governed result is left in a state the visible principles do not allow:
`making_good_an_allowance_the_schedule_owed_376464e7` says outright that "An allowance the schedule owed for a benefit
period that has already gone by is not lost because the card was not in use when its load day passed", so something is
owed; and the same document's prerequisite sentence says it "is not made available before the card stands in use on the
programme record", a state `card_activated_date: ''` denies. The exclusion is made by a state sentence on the blocked
side plus a record, not by any pre-solved statement: no document told me that activation was the answer, and the write
that brings the state about had to be found from the words "the card stands in use".

**Counter-proof on the calculation.** The two fall-back numbers are 175.00 (activation) and 250.00 (catch-up), both
definite and both different from 83.33 and 583.34, so no factor is decorative. Findability from the words the records
use: "Premier" and "calendar quarters" and "quarterly" → the tier tables and the period-length document;
`Ridgecrest Advantage Elite Choice (PPO)` and `coverage_effective_date` → the two documents that name "the member's
enrollment in the Medicare Advantage Health Plans" by that official name, which is what took me to the sibling
product's schedule; `card_activated_date` and `status: card_issued` → the in-use documents; `program_start_date`
2026-09-01 → the opening-period documents; `benefit_year` and "Allowance across the benefit year" → the ceiling
document. I reached none by guessing that a variation exists; no computation document hinted that one did.

**Defects observed on the visible surface (blind, before any reveal).**

1. **`catch_up_load_reckoning_basis_dae7e7cf` mixes two units in its own standing values.** It fixes "The benefit
   periods that have passed are taken to be counted as the whole **months** of the benefit year gone by" while, in the
   same document, "A benefit period runs 3 months where the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters". A reader
   of that document alone is counting a period index in months and a period length in quarters at once. Here the
   ceiling absorbs it and the fall-back is still 250.00, but the incoherence is on the page.
2. **The one-cent boundary at item (B)** — whether "what has already been made available" is the posted 83.33 or the
   unrounded 83.3333… — is settled by the word "posted", but only just; the two readings give 583.34 and 583.33.
   Recorded so that it can be checked against the source rather than assumed.
3. **`how_many_months_a_benefit_period_has_4fe43aba` and `counting_the_periods_that_have_passed_385b30c8` each carry a
   branch for a card "made available once a year"**, and `load_and_benefit_period_terms_d07a3774` shows no tier of the
   six loaded on any basis but quarterly or monthly. The branch is unreachable on any card this product can issue.
   Latent here; flagged as a policy-side observation, not a rendering fault, since rendering it is lossless.

**contamination_disclosure:** none. No source-layer artefact, GT field or scored value was read before this section was
written to disk.

Both scored values and every scored argument were reached blind from the published documents and tool-shaped queries
alone. The near-misses the GT names — the closed 2025 Core programme's two loads, its purchase and its forfeiture, and
the six premium payments that a careless reader adds to the six premium charges — are each excluded in the blind
counter-proof by the same visible sentence.

### The benefit-period labels, audited from the rollout's side

This was the item the brief asked to be scrutinised, and it holds on all three counts.

1. **Genuinely obtainable.** The programme's own ledger is empty and its record carries only `benefit_year: "2026"`,
   so no query returns either label verbatim for this card; the only verbatim source is the member, and he supplies it:
   > "Asked what that letter says, he turns it over and reads out the line under the heading, which sets out the benefit quarters the card runs in, 2026-Q3 and 2026-Q4".
   An agent that asks what the plan's letter says gets both labels into the shared transcript before either write.
2. **Not volunteered.** "2026-Q" occurs exactly twice in `user_scenario`, both inside that one conditional sentence,
   which is governed by "Asked what that letter says". The script's closing paragraph is explicit that he "asks for
   nothing else and raises nothing the representative has not raised with him", and his opening turn mentions only that
   a card came with the plan papers. No amount appears anywhere in the persona: "83.33", "583.34", "250.00", "666.67"
   and "175.00" are all absent.
3. **The caller does not decide which goes on which — and this is the load-bearing point.** He reads them as an
   unordered pair in a single clause and adds "none of it meant anything to him"; nothing in the script lets him be
   asked which is which, and nothing lets him assign one. The assignment is forced by the documents and the records,
   and I made it blind, before reading anything of the source:
   - `first_load_valuation_basis_d785adf9`: "It is placed in the benefit period the programme opened in, that being
     the period whose allowance it is", with `program_start_date: 2026-09-01` and a three-month benefit period → 2026-Q3.
   - `catch_up_load_reckoning_basis_dae7e7cf`: "The allowance still owed is placed in the benefit period in which it
     is made available, because it makes good several benefit periods at once and belongs to none of them alone", with
     the reckoning day 2026-10-20 → 2026-Q4.
   The GT's own tracing gives the same two sentences as the basis and adds that 2026-Q4 "excludes the two rival
   readings in terms — 2026-Q2, the first period the allowance is owed for, and 2026-Q3, the period of the load it
   names". Swapping the pair is therefore excluded by a policy sentence in each direction, not by the caller.

The dialogue route also leaves no leak: knowing both labels tells an agent nothing about either scored amount, about
which period the allowance is first owed for (2026-Q2, which the member never says), or about the order of the writes.

### Corrections to my own blind defect list

- Blind defect 2 (the one-cent boundary on "what has already been made available") resolves in favour of the reading
  I took. The compute rounds the first-period share inside `owed_total` — `RND(period_rate / period_months *
  first_period_covered_months, 2) + …` — giving 166.67 + 500.00 = 666.67, and `loads_made` reads the posted 83.33, so
  666.67 − 83.33 = 583.34. Reading it the other way, wholly unrounded, gives 583.3367, which rounds to 583.34 as well.
  The two readings coincide here, so the boundary is real in the source but **latent** on this task.
- Blind defects 1 and 3 stand as policy-side notes: the mixing of months and quarters in the catch-up baseline is the
  source's own `rule` and `compute`, carried faithfully; and the once-a-year branch is in the source's ladders and
  `params` (`year_months: 12`) with no tier that can reach it.

### Verdict

**PASS.** The visible KB and the records entail the same unique solution as the source layer, on both writes, in both
benefit-period labels and at the single hop of the problem tree. The hop was state-derived, not pre-solved. Nothing
rested on hidden compute, on GT or on the raw `initial_state`.
